annotations.title: See a sample client's claiming analysis

description: Use this tool when a financial advisor wants to see what MySSAgent's advisor analysis looks like before they have an account, or asks for an example or sample client. Needs no sign-in. Returns the stored claiming analysis for one synthetic sample household, in the same format get_client_report returns for an advisor's own client: recommended claiming ages, the benefit-by-claiming-age table computed by the MySSAgent engine from the household's earnings record, lifetime values, survivor analysis, and risk flags. The households are synthetic, labeled as samples, and are not real people. household picks one: married (a couple), widowed (a survivor case), divorced (a former-spouse benefit), single (a high earner still working). Read-only; nothing is stored.

benefit_cut.description: Optional. The benefit-cut scenario: Social Security benefits as the Trustees project they would be paid if Congress does not act before a trust fund is depleted, returned beside the scheduled figures. "trustees_oasi" is the 2026 Trustees Report projection for the Old-Age and Survivors Insurance fund (78% of scheduled benefits payable from October 2032); "trustees_combined" is the hypothetical combined retirement and disability funds (83% from July 2034); "custom" takes effective_month (YYYY-MM, 2027-01 to 2045-12) and payable_pct (50 to 100). Use it for questions about benefit cuts, trust-fund depletion or a haircut to Social Security. Payable figures, checks paid in full before the cut, and the breakeven shift come only from this parameter: they cannot be reproduced by applying a percentage to the scheduled figures, because checks paid before the effective month are paid in full. This tool prints the two Trustees presets stored with the sample's analysis.

household.description: Which sample household: married, widowed, divorced or single.
